provenance.selectionNotes: 30 real Project Gutenberg public-domain books selected across 5 real, Gutenberg-defined bookshelf genres (Gothic Fiction, Science Fiction, Adventure, Detective Fiction, Children's Literature; https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/bookshelf/39, /68, /82, /30, /20 respectively), 5-7 books per genre, sourced from live fetches of those bookshelf pages on 2026-07-17. Publication years span 1764-1929 (165 years), covering the 1700s, 1800s (every decade from the 1840s onward except the 1850s), and the 1900s-1920s, deliberately cross-cutting with genre (e.g. Gothic Fiction spans 1764-1897, Detective Fiction spans 1868-1920) so a combined genre+year facet filter exercises real facet intersection rather than two independent single-value filters. One book, Kidnapped, carries two genres (Adventure and Children's Literature) because it appears on both corresponding Gutenberg bookshelves. 5 of the 30 excerpts are verbatim quotes fetched directly from the book's actual Project Gutenberg plain-text file (Frankenstein, Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, Dracula, Treasure Island); the remaining 25 are faithful short summaries of the book's actual opening scene/premise written from well-documented plot knowledge, not verbatim Gutenberg text, per the source selection decision note's documented allowance. See docs/superpowers/notes/2026-07-17-gutenberg-facets-source-selection.md for full sourcing detail.

review.method: Maintainer review of every normalized document, query, grade, rationale, and measured top-five result.

documents.title: The Castle of Otranto
documents.description: The 1764 novel widely credited with founding the Gothic fiction genre, framed as a rediscovered medieval Italian manuscript of supernatural doom in a haunted castle.
documents.body: A gigantic helmet, fallen from nowhere, crushes young Conrad on the morning of his wedding, and his father Manfred, prince of Otranto, desperate to preserve his line, resolves to divorce his wife and marry his dead son's betrothed himself — setting off a chain of supernatural portents and buried secrets tied to an ancient prophecy about the castle's rightful owner.

documents.title: The Mysteries of Udolpho
documents.description: A hugely influential 1794 Gothic romance following the orphaned Emily St. Aubert's imprisonment in a remote, sinister Apennine castle by her sinister guardian Montoni.
documents.body: After her father's death, Emily is placed under the guardianship of her aunt's new husband, the brooding Signor Montoni, who removes her to his decaying castle of Udolpho in the Apennines, where locked rooms, black veils, and half-glimpsed horrors torment her before every apparent supernatural event is given a rational explanation.

documents.title: Frankenstein; or, the Modern Prometheus
documents.description: Mary Shelley's 1818 novel of Victor Frankenstein and the sapient creature he assembles and then abandons, often cited as an early work of science fiction as well as Gothic horror.
documents.body: You will rejoice to hear that no disaster has accompanied the commencement of an enterprise which you have regarded with such evil forebodings. I arrived here yesterday, and my first task is to assure my dear sister of my welfare and increasing confidence in the success of my undertaking. I am already far north of London, and as I walk in the streets of Petersburgh, I feel a cold northern breeze play upon my cheeks, which braces my nerves and fills me with delight.

documents.title: Wuthering Heights
documents.description: Emily Brontë's 1847 novel of the destructive, obsessive love between Heathcliff and Catherine Earnshaw across two generations on the Yorkshire moors.
documents.body: The new tenant of Thrushcross Grange, Mr. Lockwood, visits his reclusive landlord Heathcliff at the wild, isolated farmhouse of Wuthering Heights, and is given shelter overnight in a room where he finds a dead child's diary and is visited by what may be the ghost of Catherine Earnshaw scratching at the window.

documents.title: The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde
documents.description: Stevenson's 1886 novella of the respectable Dr. Jekyll's scientific experiments to separate his good and evil natures, unleashing the monstrous Mr. Hyde.
documents.body: The lawyer Mr. Utterson investigates his friend Dr. Jekyll's strange new will, which leaves everything to one Edward Hyde, a man Utterson's cousin describes witnessing trample a child in the street with cold, deliberate cruelty — the first thread in Utterson's growing suspicion that Hyde is blackmailing, or worse, controlling, Jekyll.

documents.title: Dracula
documents.description: Stoker's 1897 epistolary novel of the vampire Count Dracula's journey from Transylvania to England and the group who hunt him.
documents.body: Left Munich at 8:35 P. M., on 1st May, arriving at Vienna early next morning; should have arrived at 6:46, but train was an hour late. Buda-Pesth seems a wonderful place, from the glimpse which I got of it from the train and the little I could walk through the streets.

documents.title: A Journey to the Centre of the Earth
documents.description: Verne's 1864 novel of Professor Lidenbrock, his nephew Axel, and their guide Hans descending through an Icelandic volcano into a vast subterranean world.
documents.body: Professor Otto Lidenbrock deciphers an ancient coded manuscript that reveals the route to the centre of the Earth through the crater of the extinct Icelandic volcano Snæfellsjökull, and sets off at once with his reluctant nephew Axel to make the descent before the one day of the year when the shadow points the way.

documents.title: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
documents.description: Verne's 1870 novel of Captain Nemo and his advanced submarine Nautilus, as seen through the eyes of the marine biologist he takes captive.
documents.body: Professor Aronnax joins an expedition to hunt down a mysterious sea monster that has been ramming ships, only to discover it is in fact the Nautilus, an extraordinary submarine commanded by the enigmatic, embittered Captain Nemo, who takes Aronnax and his companions prisoner beneath the waves.

documents.title: The Mysterious Island
documents.description: Verne's 1875 novel of five Civil War-era prisoners who escape by balloon and must rebuild civilization from scratch on a deserted Pacific island.
documents.body: Five men escape a Confederate prison camp by commandeering a hot-air balloon during a storm, only to be blown far off course and crash-land on an uncharted island in the Pacific, where engineer Cyrus Harding leads them in ingeniously recreating, tool by tool, the comforts of the civilization they left behind.

documents.title: A Princess of Mars
documents.description: Burroughs's 1912 novel (first of the Barsoom series) following Confederate veteran John Carter's inexplicable transportation to Mars, where he becomes a warrior among its Martian races.
documents.body: Trapped in a cave while fleeing hostile Apaches, John Carter finds himself suddenly transported across space to Mars — known to its inhabitants as Barsoom — where Earth's lower gravity gives him superhuman strength among the green four-armed Tharks and draws him into the fate of the captive red Martian princess Dejah Thoris.

documents.title: The Dunwich Horror
documents.description: Lovecraft's 1929 weird-fiction novella (from the pulp magazine "Weird Tales") about the monstrous, otherworldly offspring of the deformed Wilbur Whateley in rural Dunwich, Massachusetts.
documents.body: In the decaying New England hamlet of Dunwich, the sinister and precociously monstrous Wilbur Whateley grows to manhood at an unnatural rate under his grandfather's occult tutelage, while townsfolk whisper about strange noises from the Whateley farm and a twin sibling no one is ever permitted to see.

documents.title: The Count of Monte Cristo
documents.description: Dumas's 1844 novel of Edmond Dantès, wrongly imprisoned by the machinations of jealous rivals, who escapes to claim a hidden fortune and enact an elaborate revenge.
documents.body: On the eve of his wedding and promotion to captain, the young sailor Edmond Dantès is denounced on false charges of Bonapartist conspiracy by three men jealous of his fortune, and is thrown without trial into the island fortress of the Château d'If, where he will spend fourteen years before an old prisoner's secret gives him both an escape route and a buried treasure.

documents.title: Around the World in Eighty Days
documents.description: Verne's 1873 novel of the punctilious Englishman Phileas Fogg, who wagers his entire fortune that he can circumnavigate the globe in eighty days.
documents.body: The precise, unflappable Phileas Fogg bets his fellow members of the Reform Club twenty thousand pounds that he can travel around the world in exactly eighty days, and sets off that very evening with his newly hired French valet Passepartout, unaware that a Scotland Yard detective is trailing him as a suspected bank robber.

documents.title: King Solomon's Mines
documents.description: Haggard's 1885 novel of hunter Allan Quatermain leading an expedition into uncharted African territory in search of a lost friend and the legendary treasure of King Solomon.
documents.body: The veteran hunter Allan Quatermain is hired by Sir Henry Curtis and Captain Good to help find Sir Henry's missing brother, last seen heading into unexplored African country in search of the fabled diamond mines of King Solomon, guided by an old map drawn in blood.

documents.title: Kidnapped
documents.description: Stevenson's 1886 historical adventure novel following young David Balfour, cheated of his inheritance, kidnapped onto a ship, and shipwrecked into the Scottish Highlands during the Jacobite unrest.
documents.body: Orphaned David Balfour arrives at his uncle Ebenezer's house expecting to claim his inheritance, only to be lured aboard a ship, knocked unconscious, and sold into indentured servitude bound for the Carolinas — until a shipwreck off the Scottish coast throws him together with the Jacobite outlaw Alan Breck Stewart.

documents.title: The Call of the Wild
documents.description: London's 1903 novel following the sled dog Buck as he is stolen from a comfortable California home and forced to adapt to the brutal life of the Klondike Gold Rush.
documents.body: Buck, a large and pampered dog living on a California estate, is stolen by a gardener's assistant and sold into the harsh world of Yukon sled-dog teams during the gold rush, where he must relearn the primitive law of club and fang to survive.

documents.title: Tarzan of the Apes
documents.description: Burroughs's 1912 novel of an English infant orphaned in the African jungle and raised by great apes, who grows into the legendary Tarzan.
documents.body: After his parents, marooned English aristocrats, die in the West African jungle, the infant John Clayton is adopted and raised by the she-ape Kala among a tribe of great apes, growing into a man of extraordinary strength and cunning who comes to be known as Tarzan.

documents.title: The Moonstone
documents.description: Collins's 1868 novel, often called one of the first detective novels in English, about the theft of a cursed Indian diamond from an English country house.
documents.body: A magnificent yellow diamond looted from an Indian temple, bequeathed to young Rachel Verinder as a birthday gift, vanishes from her bedroom the very night it is given to her, drawing the shrewd Sergeant Cuff into a case complicated by three mysterious Indian jugglers, a smear of wet paint, and a household full of secrets.

documents.title: A Study in Scarlet
documents.description: Doyle's 1887 novel, the first Sherlock Holmes story, introducing Holmes and Watson as they investigate a murder in an empty London house with the word "RACHE" written in blood on the wall.
documents.body: Dr. Watson, newly returned wounded from the Afghan campaign, takes rooms at 221B Baker Street with the eccentric Sherlock Holmes, and is soon drawn into Holmes's investigation of a well-dressed stranger found dead in an abandoned house with no visible wound and a single German word scrawled above him in blood.

documents.title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
documents.description: Doyle's 1892 collection of twelve short stories, the first Sherlock Holmes anthology, opening with "A Scandal in Bohemia."
documents.body: To Sherlock Holmes she is always _the_ woman. I have seldom heard him mention her under any other name. In his eyes she eclipses and predominates the whole of her sex. It was not that he felt any emotion akin to love for Irene Adler. All emotions, and that one particularly, were abhorrent to his cold, precise but admirably balanced mind.

documents.title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
documents.description: Doyle's 1902 novel in which Holmes and Watson investigate a supposed family curse and a spectral hound stalking Dartmoor.
documents.body: Dr. Mortimer consults Holmes about the sudden death of his friend Sir Charles Baskerville, found dead with an expression of terror on his face near the footprints of an enormous hound, and about the old family legend of a curse tied to a phantom beast that now threatens Sir Charles's heir.

documents.title: The Innocence of Father Brown
documents.description: Chesterton's 1911 collection of short stories introducing the unassuming Catholic priest-detective Father Brown, opening with "The Blue Cross."
documents.body: A famous French detective, Valentin, travels to London chasing the master criminal Flambeau, and by following a trail of small, seemingly senseless oddities left in the wake of an unremarkable little priest, uncovers that the priest himself, Father Brown, has quietly outwitted the thief.

documents.title: The Mysterious Affair at Styles
documents.description: Christie's 1920 debut novel, introducing the Belgian detective Hercule Poirot, investigating the poisoning of a wealthy widow at her English country estate.
documents.body: When the wealthy Emily Inglethorp is found dying in convulsions at Styles Court, having apparently been poisoned, her family turns for help to a refugee Belgian ex-policeman living nearby — the meticulous, mustachioed Hercule Poirot — who begins piecing together clues from a locked door, a burnt will, and a suspiciously undisturbed coffee cup.

documents.title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow
documents.description: Irving's 1820 short story (from "The Sketch Book") of the superstitious schoolmaster Ichabod Crane and his fateful encounter with the Headless Horseman.
documents.body: The lanky, superstitious schoolmaster Ichabod Crane courts the wealthy farmer's daughter Katrina Van Tassel, rivaling the boisterous local hero Brom Bones, until a late-night ride home from a party ends with Ichabod pursued through the woods by the legendary headless horseman said to haunt Sleepy Hollow.

documents.title: A Christmas Carol
documents.description: Dickens's 1843 novella in which the miserly Ebenezer Scrooge is visited by three spirits on Christmas Eve and shown the consequences of his greed.
documents.body: On Christmas Eve, the cold-hearted miser Ebenezer Scrooge is visited by the ghost of his dead business partner Jacob Marley, who warns him that three spirits — of Christmas Past, Present, and Yet to Come — will visit him that night to show him the life he has wasted and the fate that awaits him if he does not change.

documents.title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
documents.description: Carroll's 1865 novel in which a young girl falls down a rabbit hole into a nonsensical world of talking creatures and absurd logic.
documents.body: Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank, and of having nothing to do: once or twice she had peeped into the book her sister was reading, but it had no pictures or conversations in it, 'and what is the use of a book,' thought Alice 'without pictures or conversations?'

documents.title: Little Women
documents.description: Alcott's 1868 novel following the four March sisters — Meg, Jo, Beth, and Amy — growing up in New England during and after the Civil War.
documents.body: With their father away serving as an army chaplain and money scarce, the four March sisters — practical Meg, headstrong Jo, gentle Beth, and vain young Amy — resolve, at their mother's urging, to bear their small Christmas without presents cheerfully, and instead give away their own breakfast to a poor family nearby.

documents.title: Treasure Island
documents.description: Stevenson's 1883 novel of young Jim Hawkins, a pirate's treasure map, and a voyage that brings him face to face with the duplicitous Long John Silver.
documents.body: Squire Trelawney, Dr. Livesey, and the rest of these gentlemen having asked me to write down the whole particulars about Treasure Island, from the beginning to the end, keeping nothing back but the bearings of the island, and that only because there is still treasure not yet lifted, I take up my pen in the year of grace 17—, and go back to the time when my father kept the Admiral Benbow inn and the brown old seaman with the sabre cut first took up his lodging under our roof. I remember him as if it were yesterday, as he came plodding to the inn door, his sea-chest following behind him in a hand-barrow—a tall, strong, heavy, nut-brown man, his tarry pigtail falling over the shoulder of his soiled blue coat, his hands ragged and scarred, with black, broken nails, and the sabre cut across one cheek, a dirty, livid white.

documents.title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
documents.description: Baum's 1900 novel in which a Kansas farm girl, swept away by a cyclone, journeys down the Yellow Brick Road with new friends to find a wizard who can send her home.
documents.body: A cyclone lifts Dorothy Gale's farmhouse, with Dorothy and her little dog Toto inside, out of Kansas and drops it in the strange land of Oz, killing the Wicked Witch of the East and setting Dorothy on the road of yellow brick toward the Emerald City to ask the Wizard to send her home.

documents.title: Anne of Green Gables
documents.description: Montgomery's 1908 novel of the talkative, imaginative orphan Anne Shirley, sent by mistake to an elderly brother and sister on Prince Edward Island who had asked for a boy.
documents.body: Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert, an aging brother and sister on Prince Edward Island, request an orphan boy to help with farm work, but by a mix-up at the train station receive instead Anne Shirley, a fiercely imaginative and talkative red-haired girl who Marilla at first intends to send back.
